purpose: Ordered beginner-to-advanced Java backend / product engineering interview curriculum
methodology: Progress by prerequisite and pattern; 16 existing fully worked Java exercises plus independent external-practice follow-ups. Unverified company associations are intentionally omitted. Editorially reported tags are cited, not official company data.
studyMethod: Read the data structure primer and algorithm before starting a stage.
Spend 15–25 minutes attempting a problem from scratch; write brute force and its Big-O first.
Derive an optimized invariant or recurrence, then explain it aloud and implement in Java.
Test empty/boundary/duplicate/negative/large cases when allowed; trace pointers or DP states.
Re-solve after 1, 3, 7 and 21 days without looking; mark solved only once you can explain it.
After two stages, perform one 45-minute unseen mixed problem; revisit failures.

stages.title: Foundations & Java problem solving
stages.summary: Learn to reason about inputs, invariants, loops, arrays, references, and Big-O before memorising templates.

dataStructure.name: Java arrays and strings
dataStructure.description: An array stores elements at contiguous indices; String is immutable in Java. ArrayList grows dynamically.
dataStructure.realWorld: Arrays back search results and data batches; immutable strings represent request keys.
dataStructure.operations: Array index O(1); scan O(n); append to ArrayList amortized O(1)

algorithms.name: Linear scan
algorithms.description: Visit each candidate once until the condition is met
algorithms.example: Find the largest number in [3,8,2]; update max from 3 to 8; trace small inputs by hand

algorithms.name: Big-O & invariants
algorithms.description: Estimate how the cost scales; explain what must remain true each iteration
algorithms.example: At index i, maxSoFar is the largest value among elements 0..i

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Hash maps, sets & frequency counting
stages.summary: Learn HashMap and HashSet, frequency tables, duplicate detection and lookup trade-offs.

dataStructure.name: HashMap & HashSet
dataStructure.description: HashMap stores key-to-value pairs; HashSet stores unique keys. Java hashing gives expected constant-time lookup.
dataStructure.realWorld: Indexes, caching, deduplication, feature flags, counting HTTP status codes.
dataStructure.operations: Lookup/insert/delete expected O(1); worst-case assumptions depend on collision handling

algorithms.name: Hash lookup
algorithms.description: Replace repeated scanning with a map/set lookup
algorithms.example: In [2,7,11] with target 9, store 2->0 then find 7's complement 2

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Sorting, two pointers & partitioning
stages.summary: Use sorted order to avoid nested loops; understand stable sorts, merge, quicksort and in-place partitions.

dataStructure.name: Sorted arrays
dataStructure.description: Sorting orders comparable items so two pointers can make monotonic decisions.
dataStructure.realWorld: Merging paginated feeds and reconciling sorted logs.
dataStructure.operations: Two-pointer scan O(n); sort O(n log n) typical

algorithms.name: Insertion sort
algorithms.description: Insert the next item into an already sorted prefix

algorithms.name: Merge sort
algorithms.description: Divide, recursively sort halves, and merge; needs O(n) buffer

algorithms.name: Quicksort
algorithms.complexity: O(n log n) average; O(n²) worst
algorithms.description: Partition around a pivot; recurse; pivot choice matters

algorithms.name: Dutch national flag
algorithms.description: Maintain low, mid and high partitions using swaps

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Sliding windows & prefix sums
stages.summary: Recognize contiguous segments. Know fixed versus variable windows and when negative numbers break sliding-window logic.

dataStructure.name: Prefix sum array
dataStructure.description: Prefix[i+1] stores the sum of elements 0..i. Subarray [l,r) sum = prefix[r]-prefix[l].
dataStructure.realWorld: Analytics rolling aggregates and moving time windows.
dataStructure.operations: Build O(n), range sum O(1); window scan O(n)

algorithms.name: Fixed window
algorithms.description: Subtract outgoing and add incoming when sliding

algorithms.name: Variable window
algorithms.description: Expand right, shrink left while constraint fails (requires monotonic validity)
algorithms.example: For nonnegative [2,1,3], target 4: grow then shrink

algorithms.name: Prefix sum + hashmap
algorithms.description: Track cumulative sums; look for prefix-target
algorithms.example: Prefix sum 6 and earlier sum 3 produce a subarray of 3

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Binary search & answer-space search
stages.summary: Master bounds (first/last occurrence), sorted-array invariants, rotated arrays and monotonic predicates.

dataStructure.name: Sorted indexed sequence
dataStructure.description: An indexable ordered range lets you halve the candidate interval on each decision.
dataStructure.realWorld: Database index seek; threshold tuning; capacity planning.
dataStructure.operations: Binary search O(log n); binary search on answer O(log range × check cost)

algorithms.name: Lower bound
algorithms.description: Keep [low,high) as the candidate range; move high on >= target

algorithms.name: Binary search on answer
algorithms.description: Use a monotonic yes/no predicate to find minimal feasible value
algorithms.example: Minimum ship capacity with a fixed days limit

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Linked lists & fast/slow pointers
stages.summary: Learn reference rewiring, dummy heads, cycle detection, reverse and merge; draw pointer diagrams.

dataStructure.name: Singly linked list
dataStructure.description: Each node stores a value and reference to the next node, unlike contiguous array storage.
dataStructure.realWorld: Chained queues and adjacency lists; pointer-heavy LRU designs.
dataStructure.operations: Index O(n), insert at known node O(1), scan O(n)

algorithms.name: Fast & slow pointers
algorithms.description: Move one pointer one hop and the other two hops to detect cycle or middle

algorithms.name: Pointer reversal
algorithms.description: Save next before changing next pointer to previous

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Stacks, queues & monotonic structures
stages.summary: Understand LIFO, FIFO, ArrayDeque, bracket parsing and maintaining a monotonic candidate set.

dataStructure.name: Stack / queue (ArrayDeque)
dataStructure.description: Stack removes the most recent item; queue removes the oldest. ArrayDeque supports both in Java.
dataStructure.example: stack push(1), push(2), pop()->2; queue offer(1), offer(2), poll()->1
dataStructure.realWorld: Parser nesting, undo, task queues, streaming window maxima.
dataStructure.operations: Push/pop/offer/poll amortized O(1)

algorithms.name: Monotonic stack
algorithms.description: Remove dominated values while maintaining increasing/decreasing candidates
algorithms.example: Daily temperatures: pop cooler days when a hotter day arrives

algorithms.name: Monotonic deque
algorithms.description: Discard stale indices and dominated values

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Recursion & backtracking
stages.summary: Learn call-stack frames, base cases, choose/explore/undo, pruning, permutations and subsets.

dataStructure.name: Call stack
dataStructure.description: A recursive call adds a frame holding parameters and local state; deep recursion risks StackOverflowError.
dataStructure.realWorld: Configuration search, parsers, directory walks.
dataStructure.operations: For subset enumeration O(2^n) outputs; recursion depth O(n)

algorithms.name: Backtracking
algorithms.description: Choose, recurse, then undo the choice; prune invalid partial states
algorithms.example: For [1,2], choose/exclude each number to enumerate [],[1],[2],[1,2]

algorithms.name: Divide and conquer
algorithms.description: Split into independent smaller subproblems then combine

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Binary trees & depth/breadth traversals
stages.summary: Build a mental model for nodes/edges, DFS preorder/inorder/postorder, BFS levels, height and subtree properties.

dataStructure.name: Binary tree
dataStructure.description: Each node has at most two children. BST additionally orders keys; do not confuse the two.
dataStructure.realWorld: DOM trees, ASTs, org charts, indexes.
dataStructure.operations: Visit all nodes O(n); recursion O(h) stack; BFS O(w) queue

algorithms.name: DFS recursive
algorithms.description: Choose preorder/inorder/postorder based on when node is processed

algorithms.name: BFS level order
algorithms.description: Use a queue and snapshot its length per level

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: BSTs, heaps & top-K
stages.summary: Know BST invariants, balanced versus skewed shapes, heap ordering and priority queues.

dataStructure.name: Binary search tree / binary heap
dataStructure.description: BST: left values < node < right (strict if keys unique). Heap: parent has higher priority than children, but is not fully sorted.
dataStructure.realWorld: Schedulers, recommendation feeds, finding top response times.
dataStructure.operations: Balanced BST O(log n); skewed BST O(n); heap add/poll O(log n), peek O(1)

algorithms.name: Heap select top-K
algorithms.description: Keep size-k heap of the best candidates
algorithms.example: Maintain 3 largest numbers in an incoming stream

algorithms.name: Tree inorder
algorithms.description: Inorder traversal of BST visits sorted values

stages.title: Tries & string searching
stages.summary: Store prefixes efficiently; understand trie nodes, DFS over words, and when KMP beats repeated substring matching.

dataStructure.name: Trie (prefix tree)
dataStructure.description: An edge represents a character; each node corresponds to a prefix. Memory can be larger than a hash set.
dataStructure.realWorld: Autocomplete, routing prefixes, spell check.
dataStructure.operations: Insert/search O(word length), memory O(total stored characters)

algorithms.name: Trie insertion/search
algorithms.description: Traverse one edge per character
algorithms.example: Insert cat then car; both reuse ca

algorithms.name: KMP prefix function
algorithms.description: Reuse known prefix/suffix matches after mismatch
algorithms.example: Pattern abab has a reusable ab prefix

stages.title: Intervals & greedy decisions
stages.summary: Sort by starts/ends; merge overlapping ranges; learn exchange arguments to justify local choices.

dataStructure.name: Interval list
dataStructure.description: A pair [start,end] represents a segment. Whether touching endpoints overlap depends on the question.
dataStructure.realWorld: Booking windows, CPU scheduling, calendar availability.
dataStructure.operations: Sort O(n log n), sweep O(n)

algorithms.name: Interval sweep
algorithms.description: Sort intervals then merge or select without revisiting previous ones

algorithms.name: Greedy exchange argument
algorithms.description: Prove replacing an optimal first choice with the greedy choice cannot hurt

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Graph models, BFS, DFS & grids
stages.summary: Represent edges, visited sets, adjacency lists and components; compare shortest unweighted BFS with DFS exploration.

dataStructure.name: Adjacency list
dataStructure.description: For each vertex, store neighboring vertices. Directed edges are one-way; undirected edges are two-way.
dataStructure.realWorld: Service dependencies, maps, social networks, workflow DAGs.
dataStructure.operations: BFS/DFS O(V+E), space O(V) for visited/frontier

algorithms.name: BFS
algorithms.description: Queue processes nodes in increasing path length for unweighted graphs
algorithms.example: Grid island counts use four-direction neighbor checks

algorithms.name: DFS
algorithms.description: Walk deeply before backtracking; use visited to avoid loops

stages.checkpoint: Explain the invariant, walk through one nontrivial test, state worst-case complexity, and write Java without looking at the solution.

stages.title: Topological sort, DSU & connectivity
stages.summary: Recognize prerequisites, directed cycles, connected components and disjoint-set union.

dataStructure.name: Disjoint-set union (Union-Find)
dataStructure.description: Keeps components using parent pointers; path compression and union-by-size give near-constant amortized operations.
dataStructure.example: union(A,B), union(B,C) -> A and C connected
dataStructure.realWorld: Dependency resolution, clustering, network connectivity.
dataStructure.operations: Union/find amortized O(α(n)); topo sort O(V+E)

algorithms.name: Kahn topological sort
algorithms.description: Queue zero-indegree vertices; if fewer than V removed, cycle exists
algorithms.example: Course B depends on A, emit A before B

algorithms.name: Union-find
algorithms.description: Merge roots and compress paths for connectivity queries

stages.title: Weighted graphs, shortest paths & MST
stages.summary: Differentiate Dijkstra, Bellman-Ford, Floyd-Warshall, and Kruskal/Prim with valid graph assumptions.

dataStructure.name: Weighted adjacency list
dataStructure.description: Edges store both destination and cost. Negative edges break Dijkstra's standard assumptions.
dataStructure.realWorld: Routing, delivery planning, cloud network optimization.
dataStructure.operations: Dijkstra O((V+E)log V) heap; Bellman-Ford O(VE); Floyd O(V³)

algorithms.name: Dijkstra
algorithms.description: Repeatedly settle lowest tentative nonnegative distance using min heap

algorithms.name: Bellman-Ford
algorithms.description: Relax every edge V-1 times; can detect reachable negative cycles

algorithms.name: Kruskal MST
algorithms.description: Sort edges and accept if they join different DSU components
algorithms.example: Connect sites with least total cable cost

stages.title: Dynamic programming: one dimension

dataStructure.name: DP table
dataStructure.description: Cache overlapping subproblem results instead of recomputing them, or fill answers bottom-up.
dataStructure.realWorld: Optimization, planning, throttling and sequence decisions.
dataStructure.operations: Usually O(states × transition cost) time; space O(states) or optimized

algorithms.name: Memoization
algorithms.description: Recursively cache states
algorithms.example: Ways to reach step i depends on i-1 and i-2

algorithms.name: Tabulation
algorithms.description: Fill states in dependency order

stages.title: Dynamic programming: grids, strings & knapsack
stages.summary: Practice 2D state tables, subsequences, edit distance, 0/1 knapsack, interval DP and reconstruction.

dataStructure.name: 2D DP matrix
dataStructure.description: dp[i][j] represents an answer for two prefixes or grid coordinates; transitions refer to smaller states.
dataStructure.example: LCS prefixes: dp[i][j] from dp[i-1][j-1] on equal characters
dataStructure.realWorld: Diff engines, DNA similarity, cost optimization.
dataStructure.operations: Often O(nm) time and space; rolling rows reduce memory when valid

algorithms.name: LCS
algorithms.description: If end characters match add 1 diagonally, else take max of neighbors

algorithms.name: 0/1 knapsack
algorithms.description: For each item, choose skip or take once

algorithms.name: Edit distance
algorithms.description: Take min insert/delete/replace cost per pair of prefixes

stages.summary: Learn XOR cancellation, masks, shifts, signed integers, Euclid's gcd, sieve and fast exponentiation.

dataStructure.name: Bitmask
dataStructure.description: An integer's binary digits encode independent flags or membership in a small set.
dataStructure.realWorld: Permissions, compression, protocol flags, Bloom-filter internals.
dataStructure.operations: Bit checks O(1) per machine word; gcd O(log min(a,b))

algorithms.name: XOR cancellation
algorithms.description: x XOR x=0 and x XOR 0=x

algorithms.name: Euclid GCD
algorithms.description: Replace (a,b) with (b,a%b) until b=0

algorithms.name: Sieve of Eratosthenes
algorithms.description: Mark multiples of each prime to generate primes up to n

dataStructure.name: Fenwick / segment tree
dataStructure.description: Fenwick stores prefix aggregates in O(n) space. Segment tree stores range summaries and supports updates.
dataStructure.example: Sum queries over [2,1,4,3] after point updates
dataStructure.realWorld: Live counters, range analytics, leaderboard updates.
dataStructure.operations: Build Fenwick O(n log n) naive / O(n) optimized; update/query O(log n)

algorithms.name: Fenwick update/query
algorithms.description: Jump by lowest set bit to update ancestors and collect prefix partial sums

algorithms.name: Segment tree
algorithms.description: Store aggregate per segment and recursively combine overlaps

dataStructure.example: GET(key) moves entry to head; eviction removes tail
